title: The Private Markets Tech Stack (Part 2): What’s Coming Next
summary: An AI assistant on top of five systems can't fix fragmented data. Part 2 on why AI for investment operations needs a unified data model underneath.
body_markdown:
*Part 1 looked at why fragmented, specialized systems can’t answer the cross-portfolio questions institutions actually need answered same-day. This part covers why an AI layer bolted on top doesn’t fix that, and how Mantle Portal built a unified data model instead.*


---


## Why an AI layer on top isn’t enough


The obvious response to fragmentation is to add an AI layer on top of the existing tools: an assistant that reads across five systems and summarizes what it finds.


That approach has a structural limit.


**A model can only reason as well as the data underneath it lets it,** and data spread across five schemas, five update cadences, and five definitions of “position” doesn’t become coherent just because something clever sits on top.


This isn’t hypothetical anymore, either. Anthropic’s own launch this week is a clean example of the pattern:[Claude for Financial Advisors](https://financialpost.com/technology/tech-news/anthropic-pitches-claude-tool-for-financial-advisers) bundles connectors into custodians, CRMs, and wealth-tech platforms — Schwab, BlackRock, Addepar, Envestnet, iCapital, Orion, and others — with workflow skills layered over the top of them. It’s a useful tool for the job it’s built for, and it’s a different job than ours: advisor-facing, household-level, wealth management rather than institutional LP and GP fund administration. But it’s still the assistant-on-top pattern, applied by the company best positioned to do it well. **The connectors read across the same fragmented systems that were always there; they don’t give those systems a shared data model.** That it’s happening now, from the most resourced player in the space, is the clearest sign yet that the rest of the industry will keep reaching for this option first, and the clearest sign of where its ceiling sits.


The alternative is harder and slower to build: one platform, one data model, one source of truth underneath ledger, ingestion, extraction, analytics, reporting, and CRM alike, with inference running natively across all of it rather than summarizing it after the fact.


**That’s a multi-year infrastructure bet. Most vendors haven’t made it.**


---


## Who’s already built it


**[Mantle Portal](https://withmantle.com/portal/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=private-markets-tech-stack-part-2) is the clearest test case of that future state existing today,** and the sequencing of how it got there is worth examining, because it’s a defensible answer to “why hasn’t an incumbent just done this already.”


The platform didn’t set out to build every layer of the stack at once. Capital calls, capital statements, and fund documents arrive at institutions as PDFs and emails, and turning that pile into structured, queryable data is the layer everything else depends on, so that’s where we started.


We built custom agents to log into the hundreds and hundreds of GP portals, download new documents, classify them, and extract structured data. A validation layer sits on top of that pipeline, built to catch what it doesn’t know rather than guess: known-good data passes through automatically, ambiguous transactions, like recallable distributions or payment-in-kind provisions, get flagged for review, and figures that don’t reconcile get caught as errors rather than silently ingested. **That process now handles trillions of dollars in fund assets across the hundreds and hundreds of GP portals, with extraction accuracy above 99% and no offshore extraction team.** Review is largely automated with a HITL (Human in the Loop) handling only exceptions.


For public assets, Mantle Portal also reconciles real-time custodian feeds against the auditable statements that confirm them, extracting accrued income, realized and unrealized gains, equity detail, and trade activity from custodian PDFs and tracing every figure back to source. **Feeds show current position. Statements confirm what’s actually true.** Most institutions still verify that gap manually; Mantle Portal automates it.


Only once that data layer was solid did Mantle Portal extend outward. It connected with CRMs to fold in the relationship and fundraising side of the business that typically lives in a separate system, and worked with accounting firms to extend into the ledger: the layer everything else ultimately has to reconcile against. That sequencing matters because it’s the difference between a platform that grew into four layers because the foundation could support it, and a platform that bought or bolted on four layers that don’t actually share a data model underneath the marketing.


The accounting connection is the proof point that matters most, because it’s the one other platforms can’t replicate with a dashboard. When a transaction is confirmed, Mantle Portal generates the accounting consequence: a policy-driven, balanced, reviewed journal entry in the client’s own chart of accounts and template, not a suggestion someone has to re-key. **The difference between review and transcription is the whole point.** Instead of institutions trading their general ledger system for ours, they’re trading the hours a controller spends manually converting a custodian statement into a journal entry for a five-minute review of one Mantle Portal already generated correctly.


---


*Part 3 covers which layers of the stack are worth owning and which aren’t, why this consolidation is happening now, and what a unified data model makes possible that dashboards never could.*
